page: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration operates with one thread per core, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. It incorporates modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, SHA-NI, and VAES. System memory comprises 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation designed specifically for memory-bound computational tasks.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier across both compute and memory evaluations. The system achieves 349,628.66 on multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 30,237.0. Memory throughput reaches 521.03 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 215.78 GB/sec for large writes, enabling 235.68 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. For machine learning tasks, CPU-based LLM inference demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large model architectures.

The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not allocated. Network communication relies on a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Consequently, applications depend entirely on networked block storage for persistence. In terms of cost efficiency relative to the hardware profile, the dedicated bare-metal allocation delivers high memory bandwidth and deterministic single-threaded core execution without hypervisor overhead, maximizing performance density per memory gigabyte.

Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-24xl is suited for large in-memory databases, real-time caching tiers, memory-intensive data analytics, high-concurrency compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven language model inference workflows.
